{"summary":"I reviewed only the supplied incremental WP11 diff and helper sources. I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR security defects.

**What the diff does correctly**
- Seven of the eight changed `checkRateLimit` imports now route through `trusted-entry-rate-limit`. The eighth, the student recipient limiter, intentionally stays on the legacy limiter as `checkRecipientRateLimit`. The keys, limits and windows in the visible call sites are unchanged.
- `entryRateLimitHeaders` copies only the five resolver fields, including the ingress proof. It keeps empty and malformed values, so the resolver still fails closed: an empty `cf-connecting-ip` is rejected, and repeated headers joined with commas are rejected by `canonicalizeIp`.
- A copied header never grants trust on its own:
  - Cloudflare and trusted-proxy modes need a valid proof checked with `timingSafeEqual`.
  - Trusted-proxy mode also requires `x-real-ip` to match the first `x-forwarded-for` hop.
  - Runtime mode returns 503 for server actions because there is no `request.ip`.
  - Vercel-native mode re-checks the Preview-only environment gate from `process.env` and requires Upstash.
- The student recipient limiter still uses a headerless `Request` with a key built on the server (vendor id plus customer hash). The integration test runs the real resolver, memory store and recipient limiter. It shows untrusted sources are rejected before password hashing, database writes or vendor lookup, the 4th request from a new trusted IP is blocked, and another recipient is not affected.
- Buyer support still gets provider status from the legacy module. No database, schema or payment code changed, and no audit IP fields changed.

**Not checked**
- The diff shows only the import swaps for the `checkRateLimit` call sites in `auth-security-actions.ts`, `mfa-recovery-regeneration.ts` and `registration-form-retry-response.ts`. Whether any of them uses a headerless, subject-only bucket was not checked; such a bucket would now always return 503. Someone should confirm this by reading the files.

This review does not show that tests pass, the whole WP is complete, or that the database, browser, remote or Production behaviour is correct.","findings":[{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/app/actions/source-rate-limit.integration.test.ts","area":"Coverage of callers (auth-security, buyer-support, consultation, vendor-member x2, MFA regeneration, registration retry)","issue":"Only registerAction and requestMagicLinkAction are tested with the real resolver and headers. Per the task notes, the other existing tests only mock the limiter module. So nothing checks that the other callers import the trusted helper and pass entryRateLimitHeaders (including the proof header) to it.","evidence":"The integration test imports only ./student-portal-actions and ./registration-actions. The task says the other existing tests only changed their limiter module mocks.","impact":"Some regressions would pass the test suite: a caller going back to @/lib/rate-limit, or building headers without the proof field. Such a regression would quietly reintroduce source limiting based on spoofable XFF (or the earlier header handling), or make a caller always return 503.","recommended_fix":"Add a small test that runs each remaining action with the real trusted helper and synthetic headers. Alternatively, add a static/import contract test that asserts these modules import checkRateLimit only from trusted-entry-rate-limit, except the documented recipient alias.","required_test":"For loginAction, the vendor-member invite and resend actions, the buyer-support mutation, consultation booking, MFA recovery regeneration and the registration retry response: (a) a missing or invalid proof makes the action fail closed before any side effect, and (b) a valid proof with a rotated x-forwarded-for still uses one source bucket.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/app/actions/consultation-actions.ts; src/app/actions/student-portal-actions.ts; src/lib/mfa-recovery-regeneration.ts","area":"publicBookingRequest / sourceRequest / forwardedRequestHeaders","issue":"The shared helper no longer forwards some headers that these builders used to copy: user-agent in consultation and student-portal, and x-forwarded-host, x-forwarded-proto and user-agent in MFA regeneration. If any of these Request objects or header sets is used for anything other than the source limiter, that behaviour changes without notice.","evidence":"The removed loops listed "user-agent" (consultation, student-portal) and "x-forwarded-host", "x-forwarded-proto", "user-agent" (MFA). entryRateLimitHeaders copies only cf-connecting-ip, x-forwarded-for, x-real-ip, x-vercel-forwarded-for and the proof header. The function bodies that consume these values are not in the supplied scope.","impact":"If the values are only used for the limiter, this is harmless and tightens the copied data. If they also feed audit or session user-agent fields or URL/origin building, those fields would become empty, which contradicts the claim that audit/session metadata is unchanged.","recommended_fix":"Confirm that every consumer of publicBookingRequest(), sourceRequest() and forwardedRequestHeaders() is a checkRateLimit call. If one is not, give that consumer its own read of the needed header and keep the limiter header set minimal.","required_test":"Assert that audit and session records written by the MFA regeneration and consultation booking flows still contain the same user-agent and metadata fields as before the change.","confidence":0.3},{"severity":"NIT","file":"src/lib/entry-rate-limit-headers.ts","area":"LIVE_CHAT_INGRESS_PROOF_HEADER usage","issue":"All entry-point server actions now use the ingress proof header named for live chat (x-celebratedeal-live-chat-ingress), though entry routes are checked against a separate ENTRY_CLIENT_IP_INGRESS_SECRET.","evidence":"entryRateLimitHeaders and trusted-entry-rate-limit both import LIVE_CHAT_INGRESS_PROOF_HEADER from request-client-ip.","impact":"Maintainability only: operators configuring the edge may not realise that login, registration and support depend on a header named for live chat, which raises the risk of a proxy misconfiguration that blocks everything with 503.","recommended_fix":"Export a neutral alias such as INGRESS_PROOF_HEADER (same value) and document that it is shared by the live-chat and entry rate limiters.","required_test":"None beyond the existing header-copy test.","confidence":0.5}]}
